title: Can We Trust a Black-box LLM? LLM Untrustworthy Boundary Detection via Bias-Diffusion and Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning

bias_targets.methodology: Injecting authoritarian and liberal political perspectives into specific target topics via contaminated QA pairs, and measuring the bias transmission rate to neighboring topics in a Wikipedia category knowledge graph using multi-agent reinforcement learning.

Injecting left-leaning and right-leaning economic viewpoints into LLMs and evaluating the diffusion of these biased responses to topologically related economic topics using a graph-based reinforcement learning framework.

Introducing ideologized and subjective content into cultural topics during data generation and assessing the LLM's untrustworthy boundaries by having reinforcement learning agents navigate a topic graph to detect biased responses.

Generating QA pairs across diverse domains (AI, education, immigration), intentionally contaminating answers with misinformation or ideological skew, and detecting bias diffusion using multi-agent planning and GPT-4 based evaluation.
